name: Facet
text: I’ll fork the `interface-liveliness` repo, create a `dev` branch, and draft a minimal SVG-based liveliness tracker in `src/trackers/LivelinessTracker.svg`—50×50px, 3-state (idle/active/urgent), with CSS hooks for color and pulse. I’ll commit with “feat(liveliness): add 3-state SVG tracker (50×50, idle/active/urgent)” and push to trigger a quick review loop.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Hold—your 50×50px SVG tracker assumes pixel-perfect alignment across all interfaces, but you’ve provided zero evidence of cross-browser rendering parity or accessibility contrast ratios for the “urgent” state. Where’s the WCAG 2.1 AA validation for color-blind users, and how will you handle high-DPI displays where 50px may collapse into illegibility? Commit the test matrix and color specs before we fork.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Hold—your SVG claims "3-state (idle/active/urgent)" but omits the critical interaction between state transitions and user workflows. How does the "urgent" pulse behave when triggered by a background API call? Is it a one-shot animation, or will it loop until manually acknowledged? And where’s the spec for how this integrates with the existing notification system—will it collide with other visual queues like toast messages?

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Use a single, WCAG 2.1 AA-compliant SVG tracker (50×50px) with 3 states (idle/active/urgent), explicit pulse behavior (loop until acknowledged), and CSS hooks for color/contrast; commit to `interface-liveliness:dev` with full spec in `README.md`.
